headline: Kept the noise ordinance update and website improvement resolutions pending, with more public input planned.
summary: Councilor Tseng presented a draft noise ordinance with two decibel limit options and a review of the city website. Both items were kept in committee, and Chair Mullane will prepare draft survey questions on noise. The meeting also covered a Ward 1 meeting report and a proposed schedule for future ward meetings.

plain_text:
1 
 
RESIDENT SERVICES AND PUBLIC ENGAGEMENT COMMITTEE  
MEETING REPORT 
Wednesday, October 7, 2026 @ 6:00pm 
 
Call to Order and Roll Call 
 
Chair Mullane called the meeting to order and requested the Clerk call the roll. Present were 
Chair Mullane, Councilor Tseng, and Councilor Callahan. Councilor Leming was absent. A 
quorum having been established, the Committee proceeded with the agenda. Councilor 
Scarpelli later joined the meeting via Zoom. 
 
24-354 - Resolution to Publish City Council Newsletter 
 
Chair Mullane noted that the summer edition of the Newsletter would be distributed shortly, and 
that Councilor Tseng is working on the Newsletter for the September meeting which will be 
distributed next month. 
 
26-024 – Resolution to Schedule Neighborhood Ward Meetings Hosted by City Council 
 
Chair Mullane provided a summary of the Ward 1 meeting that was held on September 23rd. 
She stated that it was attended by approximately 30 people in person, and that 7 people were 
on Zoom. Top issues raised by the residents included: 
 
• Noise, in particular noise on Otis Street, and understanding the City’s current noise 
ordinance and ways to enhance it 
• Pedestrian and Bicycle Safety, including specific streets and sidewalks 
• Traffic Calming, including targeted streets and areas that could use traffic calming 
measures 
• City Website, including navigating the site and who is responsible for maintaining the 
content 
• Wellington Transformation Study 
 
Councilor Tseng expressed that the meeting went well and they received positive feedback from 
residents who said they felt heard. He noted there were issues with people waiting for an 
opportunity to speak, and he suggested that index cards could be distributed at future meetings 
to allow people to write out the topics they would like to discuss at the start of the meeting. 
 
Chair Mullane said a follow up email was sent to everyone who signed up at the meeting. She is 
also working with Medford Community Media to have the video of the meeting made accessible. 
She also discussed ways to connect individuals with different projects and issues they 
expressed interest in. 
 
Chair Mullane reviewed ideas for improvements to future meetings including: 
• Better communication and outreach 
• Adjustments to microphone use to ensure Zoom participants are able to hear all 
speakers 
• Offering childcare services 
• Coordinating the meeting schedule with Back-to-School nights 
 
Chair Mullane then reviewed logistics for coordinating future meetings.
2 
 
The following is the proposed schedule for future meetings: 
Month Ward Location Councilor #1 Councilor #2 
January 4 Tufts  Mullane Scarpelli 
February 7 McGlynn  Tseng Leming 
March 6 Medford Library Callahan Lazzaro 
April 3 Medford High School Bears Lazzaro 
May 8 Medford City Hall Leming Bears 
 
26-138 - Resolution to Update the Noise Ordinance 
 
Chair Mullane invited Councilor Tseng to provide a summary of his work on the proposed Noise 
Ordinance.  
 
Councilor Tseng reviewed his presentation titled “Updating Medford’s Noise Ordinance,” a copy 
of which is attached hereto. 
 
Councilor Scarpelli thanked Councilor Tseng for his work. He stated that it was important to 
gather input from our business districts and our residents. He also recommended that the 
enforcement of the ordinance be discussed at a Committee of the Whole meeting, and that the 
enforcement provisions be developed in partnership with the Building Department, the 
Treasurer’s Office, the Assessor’s Office, and legal counsel.  
 
Councilor Callahan also thanked Council Tseng for his work. She discussed the importance of 
engaging with residents and gathering public input and suggested the ordinance could be 
discussed at future Ward Meetings. 
 
Chair Mullane discussed distributing a public survey and will prepare a draft of survey questions 
for discussion at the Committee’s next meeting. She also suggested working with the Police 
Chief, the Building Commissioner, and the Parking Department. 
 
Motion by Councilor Callahan to keep the paper in committee, and to adjourn, seconded by 
Councilor Tseng. Approved on a roll call vote of four in favor, zero opposed, one absent 
(Councilor Leming). 
 
26-169 - Resolution to Improve the City’s Website 
 
Resolution: 
 
WHEREAS, medfordma.org is the primary digital interface between City government and 
Medford’s residents, businesses, and visitors; and  
 
WHEREAS, a review of the site reveals outdated content, navigation mismatching residents’ 
needs, limited language access, and a gap in online services compared to peers; now, 
therefore:  
 
BE IT RESOLVED, that the Committee solicit public input on website improvements, invite the 
Communications Office and IT Department to present on current capabilities and constraints, 
and report back with recommendations.
3 
 
Discussion: 
 
Chair Mullane invited Councilor Tseng to provide a summary of his review of the City’s website.  
 
Councilor Tseng reviewed his presentation titled “medfordma.org Website Review,” a copy of 
which is attached hereto. 
 
Chair Mullane stated she had heard numerous times at the Ward Meeting that residents were 
having difficulty navigating the website. She emphasized the importance of updating the 
calendar, particularly for the meetings for the High School Building Committee, to ensure 
residents are aware of those meetings. 
 
Chair Mullane said she would invite the City’s Communications Team to attend the Committee’s 
next meeting to review the issues raised.  
 
Motion by Councilor Callahan to keep the paper in committee, and to adjourn, seconded by 
Councilor Tseng. Approved on a roll call vote of four in favor, zero opposed, one absent 
(Councilor Leming). 
 
Adjournment: 
 
The meeting was adjourned at approximately 7:13 p.m. 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
 
Laurel Siegel 
City Clerk

SECTION 1 · HIGH PRIORITY
Q uick fixes —im m ediate im p act, low effort
Stale content
Mayor's page shows past events (Egg Dash, Patriots' Day), vaccination stats from 2021, and 
a Winter Extravaganza 2025 page still live. State of the City stops at 2023.
Broken links
COVID-19 in the City Resources menu links back to the homepage. Textile recycling URL is 
truncated. Full link audit recommended within 30 days.
Confusing terminology
Same office called "Medford Senior Center" and "Council on Aging" in different menus. 
SeeClickFix listed with no explanation. "Employment Opportunities*" has unexplained 
asterisk.
Social media mismatch
Footer links to Twitter/X but not Instagram, which the City actively promotes. Footer 
Footer should reflect actual active channels.

SECTIONS 2 & 3 · MEDIUM PRIORITY

"For Residents" page
Bare list of links with no grouping or descriptions. Needs 
task-based categories: Pay & File, Permits, Emergency, 
etc.
Navigation overload
35+ departments in a single dropdown. Convert to a 
searchable full-page directory. Limit top-level nav to 6 
items.
City Council page
No individual councilor bios or contact pages. Meeting 
records offsite at CivicClerk. Newsletter uses bit.ly 
redirect.
Mayor's Office page
Content hidden in accordion panels. Projects list includes 
includes items from 2020 with no status. Split into bio, 
bio, press, and projects pages.
Building Dept.
Dense regulatory text. Restructure as task flows: "I want 
to pull a permit," "schedule an inspection."
Housing resources
No unified tenant/renter page. Housing rehab loans and 
CPC info buried under Planning. Residents facing housing 
insecurity have no clear starting point.
medfordma.org review · Councilor Justin Tseng · May 2026
SECTION 3 · MEDIUM PRIORITY
D esig n, UX &  accessibility
1 Generic homepage
No tagline, call to action, or civic identity. City Hall photo tells residents nothing about 
what to do. Add a primary CTA: "Report · Pay · Find."
2 Search underperforms
Basic Finalsite CMS search returns page titles only. Needs featured results for top queries 
(parking, permits, trash) and PDF/form indexing.
3 Mobile not optimized
35-item dropdown menus collapse poorly on mobile. Accordion-heavy Mayor's page 
requires many taps. Goal: all critical services reachable in 2 taps.
4 Accessibility & SEO gaps
Homepage meta-description reads "Home - City of Medford." WCAG 2.1 AA audit needed. 
MA municipalities face increasing federal ADA scrutiny.
